findings.because: Three points repeat the techniques primer almost word for word. (1) The emulsion rescue: "a fresh yolk or a spoon of water or mustard, and the broken sauce whisked into it" against the techniques line "start a fresh base and work the broken sauce into it slowly". (2) The tadka order: "hardy spices go into the oil early and delicate ground ones brief and late" against "the hardest seeds into hot fat first and the delicate ones last". findings.fix: Let the technique primer keep the hands. Rewrite those three spots in the lexicon as the word a cook explains, drawing only on each entry's own text. Emulsions: fat and water held as droplets by an emulsifier, the physics behind mayonnaise, hollandaise, vinaigrette and beurre blanc, and the same trick as pasta's starchy water. Toasting, Blooming & the Tadka Doctrine: fat carries spice flavor, which is why raw curry powder tastes dusty. (1) The emulsion rescue: "a fresh yolk or a spoon of water or mustard, and the broken sauce whisked into it" against the techniques line "start a fresh base and work the broken sauce into it slowly". (2) The tadka order: "hardy spices go into the oil early and delicate ground ones brief and late" against "the hardest seeds into hot fat first and the delicate ones last". problems.fix: Let the technique primer keep the hands. Rewrite those three spots in the lexicon as the word a cook explains, drawing only on each entry's own text. Emulsions: fat and water held as droplets by an emulsifier, the physics behind mayonnaise, hollandaise, vinaigrette and beurre blanc, and the same trick as pasta's starchy water. Toasting, Blooming & the Tadka Doctrine: fat carries spice flavor, which is why raw curry powder tastes dusty. Caramel Stages & Sugar Work: the syrup's temperature decides what it becomes, and wet caramel is safer while dry caramel is faster and riskier. Keep crystallization named as the saboteur without the stirring rule.

critic.notes: The Level test sentence appears in both 2-dishes and 2-techniques. I did not flag it, because tools/primers/dedupe-level-test.mjs keeps it only in the last primer that carries it (2-techniques at this level). Run that script after take.mjs. The next lines agree about Sous Chef across all eight primers (live fire and the wok, the standards that govern a service, inspection-ready, charcuterie boards, bitter and rich), and every one I checked matches neighbours.above. Items placed at more than one level agree: beurre blanc, confit, lamination, the cheese material and the flank, skirt and hanger cards. Three softer points were left alone to keep this pass bounded. (1) The plates primer stresses that the hanger is not the flank (it sits with the skirt in the short plate), while the lexicon groups them as Flank, Skirt & Hanger sharing one law. Both are true, but no primer names the difference, and a server could blur it. (2) The techniques primer does not name Scoring, which carries a written standard at this level, or Choux pastry. It does not have to name every item, but Scoring belongs with the pastry and bread marks. (3) 2-deck (536 words) and 2-service (570 words) are over the 520-word aim but inside the 650 limit. The braise gets its sear-and-color explanation in 2-dishes, 2-techniques and 2-lexicon, each from its own angle; I judged that tolerable, not a repeat.
